I think we had decided to filter out DIMM units (and other object paths ending in "unit[0-9][0-9]" from `--dumpInventory --table` option only, and process them for `--dumpInventory` JSON output. I remember someone in manufacturing had complained on this point when we had initially filtered out "unit"s from the JSON output.
Removed it, instead brought in cables. We don't need them in this case.
Acknowledged

We can pass `Inventory.Item` interface in the constraining interfaces argument, to restrict the return value to PIM interfaces only. That way we can avoid the outer `for` loop to find `inventoryManagerService`.

No, that assumption is not correct, interfaces are not restricted to services.
Any path under any service can implement an interface.

Instead of iterating over the map (O(n)), we can look up `inventoryManagerService` entry using `l_mapperResp[constants::inventoryManagerService]` (O(log n))

On second thought, `std::map.find()` would be better. 
`std::map []` performs insertion if `key` is not found.

`std::map.find()` returns `std::map.end()` if `key` is not found, else returns an iterator to requested element.
In this case it won't;
